newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-FIA SAYS FRENCH GRAND PRIX TO GO AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FIA SAYS FRENCH GRAND PRIX TO GO AHEAD.

text.p: The International Automobile Federation (FIA) said on Friday that the French Formula One Grand Prix, threatened by a row over televison coverage, would go ahead as planned on June 29 at Magny-Cours.

"The difficulties surrounding access to the French Grand Prix by unauthorised television crews have been resolved and the event is now confirmed as a round of the 1997 FIA Formula One world championship," FIA said in a statement.
The dispute over access to the Magny-Cours circuit for a local television channel had been solved, allowing the race to take place, FIA said.
The sport's ruling body said in a statement that it was grateful to French Justice Minister Jacques Toubon and Sports Minister Guy Drut for their help in the matter.
